Porting an existing NIS study to easyNIS

Source: vignettes/porting.Rmd
porting.Rmd

This short guide maps common steps in an existing NIS analysis to easyNIS. The examples use invented discharges, including records from nis_example() with illustrative diagnosis and procedure codes.

Match each code slot separately

A legacy scan that pastes slots together can match a code that never occurs in any slot. This invented record splits A123 across two diagnoses.

split_slots <- data.frame(I10_DX1 = "A1", I10_DX2 = "234")
with(split_slots, grepl("A123", paste0(I10_DX1, I10_DX2)))
#> [1] TRUE
nis_flag_dx(split_slots, eligible = "A123")$eligible
#> [1] FALSE

For patterns such as ^A12.*|^B34.*, use the prefixes c("A12", "B34"). nis_flag_dx() checks each diagnosis slot on its own. nis_flag_pr() does the same for procedure slots. Set position = "principal" to check slot 1, "secondary" to check later diagnosis slots, or "any" to check all available slots. Prefix arguments are normalized by removing periods and spaces and converting to uppercase. Slot values are compared as stored.

The example starts from generated data and substitutes illustrative codes, then creates diagnosis and procedure flags:

example_path <- nis_example(years = 2018:2020)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpQ0RqZV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

nis_flagged <- nis_open(example_path, years = 2018:2020) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    I10_DX1 = dplyr::if_else(AGE >= 50, "A1234", "A12345"),
    I10_DX2 = dplyr::if_else(FEMALE == 1, "B341", "C005"),
    I10_PR1 = dplyr::if_else(FEMALE == 1, "0AB12", "0XY34")
  ) |>
  nis_flag_dx(cohort_dx = c("A12", "B34"), position = "principal") |>
  nis_flag_dx(exposure = "B34", position = "any") |>
  nis_flag_pr(example_procedure = "0AB", position = "any")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpQ0RqZV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

Use a regex definition when the legacy rule constrains the rest of the code. This example requires exactly two digits after A12 in a diagnosis slot. Both principal codes match the prefix, while only A1234 matches the regex.

nis_flagged <- nis_flagged |>
  nis_flag_dx(eligible = list(regex = "A12[0-9]{2}"), position = "any")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpQ0RqZV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

nis_flagged |>
  dplyr::distinct(I10_DX1, cohort_dx, eligible) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   I10_DX1 cohort_dx eligible
#>   <chr>   <lgl>     <lgl>   
#> 1 A12345  TRUE      FALSE   
#> 2 A1234   TRUE      TRUE

Regex definitions match the whole stored slot, so outer ^ and $ anchors are optional. A legacy regex that intentionally matched only part of a code needs an explicit pattern for the rest of the slot, such as a trailing .* for an unconstrained suffix. Write case-sensitive patterns for the stored uppercase, undotted NIS codes. The package passes regex patterns through without the normalization applied to literal prefixes.

Replace local recode helpers

If a local cleaning helper used case_when() to turn known HCUP codes such as sex, payer, or discharge disposition into labels, remove those repeated recodes. nis_design() calls nis_label() on the collected analysis data. Known binary codes become logical, and multi-level codes become factors. Both receive variable labels. You can call nis_label() directly on a collected data frame when you need the same recoding outside nis_design().

Keep custom study-derived variables in mutate(). Set their factor order explicitly with forcats::fct_relevel(), and override the displayed label at the table where it is used:

study_design <- nis_flagged |>
  nis_design(
    cohort = cohort_dx & AGE >= 50,
    keep = c(
      AGE, FEMALE, DIED, LOS, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS,
      cohort_dx, exposure, example_procedure
    ),
    dollars = 2020
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_band = forcats::fct_relevel(
      factor(dplyr::if_else(AGE >= 65, "65 or older", "Under 65")),
      "Under 65"
    )
  )
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.

Use gtsummary label overrides for derived variables; HCUP labels already cover the common coded fields:

table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  study_design,
  by = exposure,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE, age_band, DIED, LOS, cost_adj),
  label = list(
    FEMALE ~ "Female",
    age_band ~ "Illustrative age group",
    cost_adj ~ "Hospital cost in 2020 USD"
  )
)

table_one$table_body |>
  dplyr::select(variable, label) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
#> # A tibble: 8 × 2
#>   variable label                      
#>   <chr>    <chr>                      
#> 1 AGE      Age, years                 
#> 2 FEMALE   Female                     
#> 3 age_band Illustrative age group     
#> 4 age_band Under 65                   
#> 5 age_band 65 or older                
#> 6 DIED     Died during hospitalization
#> 7 LOS      Length of stay, days       
#> 8 cost_adj Hospital cost in 2020 USD

Keep discharge disposition and mortality separate

Check source values alongside the derived outcomes and the displayed disposition label before carrying over a legacy recode.

outcomes <- nis_outcomes(data.frame(DIED = 1L, LOS = 2L, DISPUNIFORM = 6L))
outcomes[c("DIED", "DISPUNIFORM", "in_hospital_death", "discharge_disposition")]
#>   DIED DISPUNIFORM in_hospital_death discharge_disposition
#> 1    1           6              TRUE                     6
as.character(nis_label(outcomes)$discharge_disposition)
#> [1] "Home health care"

This invented row has an in-hospital death flag and a disposition label of “Home health care.” Check inconsistent pairs against the source-year coding and keep a documented rule for handling them. Use in_hospital_death for mortality and discharge_disposition for destination. See Hospitalization outcomes.

Declare the cohort with nis_design()

Older scripts may build survey::svydesign() with HOSPID and TRENDWT, then call subset() for the analysis cohort. Those fields are not available in current NIS releases. For the supported ICD-10 years, nis_design() uses HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, and DISCWT, and makes hospital and stratum IDs year-specific before combining years. Pass the cohort expression and the columns to retain; do not filter to the cohort before constructing the design.

The design retains one placeholder for each hospital-year with no cohort discharges. This lets the survey domain retain the sampled hospital context when estimating the declared cohort. The placeholder-row method is experimental and should be validated against a full-data design for the analysis at hand. After nis_design(), filters should only narrow the cohort declared by its cohort argument.

Replace charge adjustment and testing switches

If adj_TOTCHG was inflation-adjusted charges, its counterpart is charges_adj. cost_adj estimates hospital cost by multiplying charges by CCR_NIS before inflation adjustment. With TOTCHG and CCR_NIS in keep, nis_design(..., dollars = 2020) creates both fields, as in the example above. For a collected data frame, call nis_cost(data, dollars = 2020) directly.

Replace a TESTING switch that points to a small hand-picked data file with nis_example(years = 2018:2020). It writes an invented, temporary dataset with the same broad column shape needed to run the pipeline; it contains no study records.

The example directory can be removed after use with unlink(example_path, recursive = TRUE).

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Regex expressions may encode suffix rules that a prefix flag cannot reproduce. Review each code-set translation.
  • A pooled analysis needs year-scoped hospital and stratum identifiers and a stated weight convention.
  • Never treat nis_example() results as study or national estimates.

Function references: nis_open(), nis_flag_dx(), nis_flag_pr(), nis_design(), nis_cost(), and nis_suppress().
